items.defectStatement: BlockedEmail.should_block? uses a case-sensitive email lookup, allowing a submitted address with different capitalization from the stored blocked address to bypass the block list.
obligations: Match email addresses case-insensitively, including existing mixed-case stored addresses.
Preserve exact address matching apart from case; do not introduce wildcard matching.
Preserve match statistics updates and the distinction between block and do_nothing actions.
items.notes: Lowercasing only the input is insufficient because stored addresses are not normalized. Normalizing stored values is optional for this defect when the lookup compares both sides case-insensitively.

items.defectStatement: The domain restriction matcher accepts a configured domain followed by additional characters, allowing user@example.com.evil.com through an example.com whitelist and incorrectly rejecting it under the corresponding blacklist. It also treats regex metacharacters other than dots in configured domains as regex syntax.
obligations: Require the configured domain to end at the absolute end of the email address.
Treat each pipe-separated domain as literal text.
Preserve case-insensitive matching and support for multiple configured domains.
Preserve the existing whitelist and blacklist decision flow.
items.exampleFix:
def email_in_restriction_setting?(setting, value)
    domains = setting.split('|').map { |domain| Regexp.escape(domain) }.join('|')
    regexp = Regexp.new("@(?:#{domains})\\z", Regexp::IGNORECASE)
    value =~ regexp
  end
items.notes: Use an absolute end anchor; Ruby's $ also matches before a newline. Escape domains individually so the pipe separator still represents alternatives.

items.defectStatement: emailValidation treats every previously server-rejected address as permanently invalid because rejectedEmails is never cleared. Consequently, a later server-side policy change cannot make that address submitable again during the controller's lifetime.
obligations: Allow a previously rejected address to be submitted again for current server-side validation.
Preserve blank-address, email-format, and authenticated-email validation.
Preserve server-side rejection handling and its displayed error message.
items.notes: Deleting the cited cache-based veto is a valid local fix: server failures still display through flash, while cached rejections cease disabling submission. Retaining temporary field-level rejection feedback through input-change or modal-reset invalidation would require changes outside this anchor.
